title: Leveraging Hybrid Classical-Quantum Methods for Efficient Load Rebalancing in HPC
problem: Load imbalance in parallel HPC applications occurs when processes have different execution times, causing faster processes to wait at synchronization points. The Load Rebalancing Problem (LRP) requires determining which tasks to migrate between processes to balance computational load.
motivation: Load imbalance reduces parallel efficiency and increases synchronization overhead in HPC applications, making it a critical performance optimization target.
method: When parallel processes finish at different times, faster ones wait at synchronization points, causing delays. The paper solves this by formulating load balancing as a quadratic optimization problem (a math problem certain computers can solve using quantum techniques), creating two versions that trade off between needing fewer quantum bits versus having simpler constraints. The hybrid approach—combining classical and quantum computation—is tested against three traditional heuristic methods (Greedy, Karmarkar-Karp, and ProactLB), measuring success by imbalance ratio, speedup achieved, and task migration count.
key_novelty: It uses hybrid classical-quantum computation to solve load rebalancing through constrained quadratic formulations.
contributions: Formulation of load rebalancing problem as constrained quadratic models suitable for quantum computation
Two quantum algorithm variants with different tradeoffs between qubit requirements and constraint types
Demonstration that quantum methods achieve 4x reduction in task migrations compared to classical heuristics
Comparative evaluation framework benchmarking quantum versus classical load balancing approaches

metrics.speedup: Up to 4x reduction in task migrations compared to classical methods
